what_worked: Investment-memo framing with falsification conditions turns a dataset exercise into a genuine decision document.
fix_next: Reconcile the revenue field used throughout—every dollar figure is ~8-9x the reference total, suggesting a field-mapping error.
verdict: Exceptional storytelling and structure undermined by systematic revenue-field mismatch across every slide.
factual_error_detail: Slides 1-7,12: total revenue $133.8M vs reference $15.6M (~8.6x). Slide 12: Stripe $119.91M vs ref $13.5M; RevenueCat $6.83M vs ref $1.3M; Dodo $0.32M vs ref $0.039M. Slide 10: AI total $18.43M vs ref $2.36M, Marketing $14.64M vs ref $1.32M; AI median $4,301 vs ref $503, Marketing median $10,028 vs ref $2,370. Slide 5: anonymous revenue share 21% vs ref 26.5%.

evidence.insight: Slides 7-8 reframe the platform as '200 businesses plus 800 profiles'—genuinely decision-useful. Slide 15 identifies ARR-vs-trailing anchoring with rank-correlation evidence. Slide 16 builds an actionable acquisition screen with specific company-level data. Slide 14 derives a two-track operational model from the barbell distribution.
evidence.narrative: Tight investment-memo arc: thesis→data audit→KPIs→concentration→segmentation→growth→risk→marketplace→opportunity→recommendations→roadmap→conclusion→appendix. Every slide title is an assertion. Conclusion includes explicit falsification conditions. Sequencing footnote on slide 18 shows deliberate ordering.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 sets audience (investment committee), question (invest or not), scope (1,000-row frozen extract). Slide 5 audits data quality before making claims. Footnotes consistently distinguish fact from interpretation (e.g., 'competitive read is the author's'). Limitations flagged throughout including 'no historical transaction record.'
evidence.accuracy: Structural counts are correct: 636 Stripe, 129 anonymous, 241 missing country, 288 missing audience, 274 missing category, 216 zero-revenue. Top-10 share 50.6% close to ref 49.6%. However, every revenue figure is systematically ~8-9x the reference total ($133.8M vs $15.6M), propagating through Stripe, RevenueCat, Dodo, and all category totals/medians. Anonymous share stated as 21% vs reference 26.5%.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/gold palette with clear hierarchy. Every slide has section label, assertion title, chart, and interpretation panel. Charts are appropriately simple. Slide 8 truncated y-axis (185-215) slightly exaggerates uniformity. Slide 15 scatter is well-annotated with base notes and outlier handling disclosed.
evidence.ai_slop: None detected—every claim is dataset-specific, footnotes distinguish fact from assumption, no generic filler or inflated language.

change_reason: Reduced accuracy from 6.0 to 5.5; the systematic revenue-field mismatch affects the headline figure on nearly every slide and cascades into category totals, provider breakdowns, and marketplace economics. Structural counts and ratios are correct, preventing a lower score.
